lab_title: Virtual Cardiology: Anatomy of the Heart and Pathway of Blood Flow
top_level_objectives: Identify the four chambers, four valves, and major blood vessels of the human heart.
Trace the sequential pathway of deoxygenated and oxygenated blood through the pulmonary and systemic circulation loops.
Explain the functional relationship between myocardial wall thickness and the pressure demands of systemic versus pulmonary circulation.
Describe how the cardiac valves prevent backflow to ensure unidirectional blood flow during the cardiac cycle.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the student to the external landmarks of the heart and the major vessels entering and leaving the cardiac base.
key_visuals: A high-fidelity 3D model of a beating human heart positioned in the center of the workspace.
Color-coded, glowing highlights on the superior/inferior vena cava, pulmonary trunk, pulmonary veins, and aorta.
Text labels identifying the anterior and posterior surfaces.
student_actions: Rotate and scale the heart model to observe its orientation in the thoracic cavity.
Tap on each major blood vessel to reveal its name and whether it carries blood to or away from the heart.
Categorize the highlighted vessels into incoming (venous) and outgoing (arterial) channels using a virtual sorting board.

scenes.brief_purpose: Explore the four internal chambers of the heart, focusing on their spatial relationships and structural differences.
key_visuals: A coronal cross-section view of the 3D heart model, exposing the interior lumens.
Visual boundaries delineating the right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, and left ventricle.
Text descriptions highlighting chamber characteristics like the pectinate muscles and trabeculae carneae.
student_actions: Inspect the internal spaces of all four chambers by peering into the open cross-sectional AR model.
Place color-coded virtual flags (blue for deoxygenated, red for oxygenated) in the appropriate chambers.
Complete a matching activity that pairs each of the four chambers with its physiological description.

scenes.brief_purpose: Examine the structural anatomy of the four heart valves and understand their mechanism of preventing backflow.
key_visuals: Close-up, interactive models of the atrioventricular valves (tricuspid and mitral) with visible chordae tendineae and papillary muscles.
Close-up models of the semilunar valves (pulmonary and aortic).
A dynamic animation loop showing the valves opening and closing in response to the cardiac cycle.
student_actions: Manipulate a timeline slider to slow down the heartbeat, observing when the AV valves open relative to the semilunar valves.
Tap on the papillary muscles and chordae tendineae during ventricular contraction to see how they prevent AV valve prolapse.
Identify and label each of the four valves based on their anatomical location and leaflet count.

scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the pathway of deoxygenated blood returning from the body, through the right side of the heart, and out to the lungs.
key_visuals: Blue animated flow particles entering through the vena cavae, moving into the right atrium, passing through the tricuspid valve, into the right ventricle, and exiting through the pulmonary valve and arteries.
A schematic mini-map of the body showing the position of the heart relative to the lungs.
student_actions: Arrange a series of anatomical labels in the correct chronological order to map the flow of deoxygenated blood.
Interact with the blue flow particles to trigger transitions through each valve, observing how the valve flaps react to the forward flow.

scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the pathway of oxygenated blood returning from the lungs, through the left side of the heart, and out to the rest of the body.
key_visuals: Red animated flow particles entering through the pulmonary veins, filling the left atrium, passing through the mitral valve, entering the left ventricle, and surging past the aortic valve into the aorta.
A schematic mini-map showing the blood circulating from the aorta to the systemic body tissues.
student_actions: Draw the pathway of oxygenated blood directly onto the AR model using a virtual digital pointer.
Identify the points of transition where blood changes from high-carbon-dioxide to high-oxygen content.
Answer multiple-choice checkpoint questions to reinforce the sequence of structures from the lungs back to systemic circulation.

scenes.brief_purpose: Analyze the structural differences between the left and right ventricular walls and relate this to the pressure requirements of their respective circuits.
key_visuals: A side-by-side comparative cross-section highlighting the thick myocardium of the left ventricle and the thinner myocardium of the right ventricle.
A simulated pressure gauge visualization showing the high pressure required for systemic circulation versus the low pressure needed for pulmonary circulation.
student_actions: Use an interactive AR caliper tool to measure and record the wall thickness of both the right and left ventricles.
Drag pressure and distance labels to the corresponding ventricle to connect physical muscle thickness with biological workload.
Formulate a brief hypothesis within the app explaining why a patient with systemic high blood pressure might develop left ventricular hypertrophy.
